classification.difficultyReason: The radius (6 cm) and slant height (14 cm) are both given, so parts a and b are direct substitutions into 2πr² and πrl, with no Pythagoras step and no diameter-to-radius conversion. Part c is scaffolded by the two earlier parts and by the wording 'curved surface area', so the student just adds the two results. The only extra step is recognising that the shared circular face is internal, which the earlier parts already imply. This is slightly more than the single-formula sphere calculations in p20-q1, because it involves two different formulas and a combining step. It is easier than p20-q3, which needs a rearranged formula and an inverse square root, and easier than p14-q3, which needs Pythagoras to find the slant height.

content.prompt: A hemisphere sits on a cone as shown. Give answers correct to 1 decimal place.

answer.worked:
The shared circular face is internal, so only the two curved surfaces are included.
$$\begin{align*}A&=72\pi+84\pi\\&=156\pi\\&\approx490.1\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
